title: Scarless Introduction of Point Mutations in Mammalian Cells with S. pyogenes Cas9
author: Malvika Tejura
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.xuyfnxw

steps.title: Design sgRNAs
steps.instruction: Design 3-4 sgRNAs to identify the one with the highest cutting efficiency at the mutation site.

substeps.instruction: Download the genomic DNA (gDNA) transcript of the gene (e.g., using Benchling), ensuring genomic DNA is used rather than cDNA or mRNA to include introns.
Locate the mutation site of interest in the gDNA transcript.
Identify the PAM sequence (NGG for S. pyogenes Cas9 on the + strand; CCN on the - strand).
Ensure the double-stranded break (3 nucleotides 5' of the PAM) is as close as possible to the mutation site, ideally within 10 nt.
Select a 20-nucleotide protospacer/target sequence adjacent to the PAM.
Verify guide designs at synthego.com.
In vitro transcribe the guides or order them from a supplier (e.g., Synthego).

steps.title: Test sgRNA Cutting Efficiency
steps.instruction: Nucleofect the sgRNAs into target cells to determine the most efficient guide using ICE analysis.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend sgRNAs to 200uM in TE buffer.

Nucleofect RNPs into cells following a suitable protocol (e.g., for N2A cells: program Neuro2a-HE for 4D Lonza nucleofector in SF cell line solution; for iPSCs: program CB-150 for 4D Lonza nucleofector in P3 Primary solution, using Rock inhibitor during centrifugation and plating as needed).
Allow cells to recover for two days.
Extract genomic DNA from nucleofected cells.
Perform PCR with appropriate primers, purify the product, and send for sequencing.
Analyze sequencing data using Synthego's ICE analysis tool to select the sgRNA with the highest score.

steps.title: Design Single Stranded Repair Templates
steps.instruction: Design an asymmetric 120 nt repair template based on the selected sgRNA to maximize knock-in efficiency.

substeps.instruction: Identify the target strand (the strand opposite the PAM/target sequence that hybridizes with the sgRNA).

Design the template as a modification of the target strand with an asymmetric 90:30 nt split: 30 nts binding the 5' end of the double-stranded break and 90 nts binding the 3' end (or vice versa depending on the target strand).
Incorporate the desired mutation into the template.

Introduce a silent mutation to change the PAM sequence to prevent Cas9 from cutting the repair template. If not possible, introduce 2-3 silent mutations in the target sequence, prioritizing mismatches closer to the PAM.

steps.title: Design and Validate Genotyping Primers
steps.instruction: Create and test PCR primers to flank the mutation site for genotyping.

substeps.instruction: Design 4-5 sets of primers (e.g., using NCBI primer blast) to produce a product of approximately 500 bp, ensuring the size is >120 bps to avoid amplifying the repair template.
Perform gradient PCR using genomic DNA and a DNA polymerase of choice for all primer sets.
Analyze products on an agarose gel to select the best primer set and annealing temperature (characterized by a single well-defined band).

steps.title: Perform Knock-in Nucleofection
steps.instruction: Nucleofect cells with the best sgRNA and the repair template.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend the repair template to 100uM in TE buffer.
Nucleofect cells with both the RNP and the repair template using the previously established nucleofection protocol.
Allow cells to grow for two days.
Extract genomic DNA from a portion of the cells, freeze some cells, and dilute others for cloning.
PCR the extracted gDNA, purify, and sequence the product.
Analyze pool knock-in (KI) efficiency using Synthego's Knock-in efficiency tool (typical high efficiency is 30-50%).

steps.title: Generate and Screen Single Cell Clones
steps.instruction: Isolate single cell clones and verify the successful introduction of the point mutation.

substeps.instruction: If pool KI efficiency is sufficient, serially dilute cells into a 96 well plate (or use FACS to sort single cells if cells are 'clumpy').
Allow cells to grow for one to two weeks.
Pick single cell clones and replate them into a 24 well plate.
Once confluent, extract genomic DNA from a portion of the cells and propagate the remainder.
Perform PCR on the gDNA, purify, and sequence the product.
Analyze the results using Synthego's KI analysis tool to verify the mutation in each cell line.
